data.title: Schools shuttered as student protests sweep through France

data.title: Putin's escalating bombing campaign won't break Ukrainians' resolve. History shows that it's doomed to fail | Rajan Menon
data.description: As winter approaches and the fifth anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion looms, it’s worth remembering that this mode of warfare rarely crushes morale Vladimir Putin’s army hasn’t made much headway in Ukraine this year, and his territorial goals – annexing four Ukrainian provinces – remain elusive, despite more than four and a half years of war. That explains his recent efforts to sap Ukrainians’ will to resist by launching relentless drone and missile strikes against their cities – targeting, among other sites, residential buildings, large open-air markets, shopping malls, the Dobrobut medical centre and the National Academy of Sciences, both in Kyiv. The capital has been hit the hardest, but other cities – Dnipro , Kharkiv, Kherson, Odesa , Mykolaiv, Sumy – haven’t been spared. Air-raid sirens pierce the quiet of night. People scramble to shelters (assuming there are any nearby) or, in Kyiv, race to below-ground subway stations. Even walking along city streets, shopping, or filling up your car at a garage forecourt – which are prime targets – can lead to injury, or even death. Rajan Menon is a professor emeritus of international relations at the City College of New York and a senior research scholar at Columbia University’s Saltzman Institute of War and Peace Studies Continue reading...

data.title: My search for the perfect Italian aperitivo in Verona
data.description: The classic pre-dinner drink and snack combo varies depending where you are in Italy. In this fair city, it’s an institution that can even be enjoyed first thing I arrived in Verona, I admit, without a particularly clear idea of what aperitivo meant. In Italy, the ritual – broadly, a drink and something small to eat before a meal – speaks a different dialect in every city. Milan has turned it into a polished after-work institution. In Venice, it is more itinerant: an ombra (a small glass of wine) along with a cicchetto (a bite-size snack) and then on to the next bacaro (one of the city’s traditional wine bars). Verona follows another logic. Continue reading...

data.title: Pasture lives: the rebel cheesemakers preserving an Alpine tradition
data.description: A story of storico ribelle, produced by a small group of mountain herders according to a traditional farming system based on seasonal and rotational grazing My journey into the world of storico ribelle began with a shared passion for photography and the mountains. A close friend of mine lives in the Orobie Alps . He loves the mountains and the natural environment that surrounds him, and we share the same passion for photography. When I finally went to visit him, I discovered a way of experiencing the mountains that was very different from the one I knew growing up in the Apennines, where I come from. What struck me was not only the landscape, but the relationship people still have with it. Here, I discovered a world where the mountain is not simply a place to visit or explore, but a place to live and work. A world where cheese is still a tradition rather than an industrial product, and where the rhythms of the seasons, the animals and the daily work of the alpeggiatori – the mountain herders – are still deeply connected. Continue reading...

data.title: To cull or not to cull: Greenland debates fate of world’s slowest shark
data.description: As trawlers compete with Greenland sharks for halibut and cod, conservationists and fishers clash over what to do about misunderstood species ‘When I accidentally catch a shark, I bring it to my dogs,” Henrik Jensen, a 27-year-old from Greenland’s west coast, says casually. “I don’t let it back down because [the sharks] bully me and cut my lines.” Jensen has fished for halibut in Ilulissat, Greenland’s third largest town, for a decade. He works an hour north of the town’s main iceberg-laden fishery, which sustains the livelihood of nearly 400 fishers. There, the halibut are bigger and more plentiful, but so are the Greenland sharks. Continue reading...

data.title: My sister Nicole married OJ Simpson. This is what I wish I had known
data.description: Since Nicole Brown Simpson’s murder in 1994, Denise Brown has devoted herself to ending domestic violence. She talks about her beloved sister, the trauma she witnessed in the couple’s marriage and how lives can be saved The last night Denise Brown spent with her sister Nicole Brown Simpson was at a restaurant for a family celebration. Nicole looked out of the window. “All of a sudden she goes, ‘Oh my God, there he is.’ He was driving by.” Brown looked out, trying to get a glimpse of her sister’s ex-husband, the former American football star OJ Simpson. “I saw these headlights. She said, ‘He’s constantly following me.’” They went back to talking about their plans for the summer. The following morning, 13 June 1994, Brown was up early at her parents’ house in Orange County in southern California, when the phone rang shortly after 6am. “I heard my mom scream a scream that I had never heard from a human being,” says Brown. “It was so guttural. Just awful.” Continue reading...

data.title: Brazil’s presidential race goes to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
data.description: Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro put in a stronger than expected showing, with Lula calling the result ‘unexpected’ Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff. With 99.9% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 45.1%. Bolsonaro received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m. Continue reading...

data.title: Internet Watch Foundation reports huge rise in AI child sexual abuse material
data.description: Abuse material monitor says number of AI images assessed this year is already 40% higher than last year’s total AI-generated child sexual abuse material is proliferating online, with the amount of illegal material investigated this year already exceeding the total for 2025. Analysts at the Internet Watch Foundation have found more photorealistic child sexual abuse material in the first half of 2026 than for the whole of the prior year. The UK-based IWF, which monitors abuse material globally, said it had assessed 6,310 AI images that met the legal definition of child sexual abuse, 40% higher than last year’s total of more than 4,500. data.title: Revealed: the methane mega-leaks from UN climate summit host Turkey
data.description: Exclusive: Cop31 leader calling for global curbs on climate-heating gas has landfills producing some of world’s worst plumes Two or three nights each week, the smell descends. Residents of villages on the rural outskirts of Istanbul don’t know what the smell is, but they have been plagued by it for years: a smell so bad they have to sleep with their windows closed even during hot summer nights. They know the source, too: the huge Silivri municipal waste dump a few miles away that is belching out stinking gases as food and other organic waste rots. “The smell is not subtle. It suffocates you,” said Kemalettin Özenç, sitting outside a tea shop in the village of Yolçatı. “It’s worse when the air is still: sometimes families linger until midnight out here. Even when you go inside it’s inescapable.” Continue reading...

data.title: Tom Cruise’s Digger has flopped spectacularly – but I think it is a misunderstood masterpiece
data.description: Alejandro G Iñárritu’s film may be about to become one of the biggest bombs Hollywood has ever seen – but it is destined to be re-evaluated with time This article contains spoilers for Digger I feel for film critics, I really do. Tom Cruise’s latest film Digger put them in an impossible position: you can’t really talk about it without spoiling what makes it, in my eyes, a masterpiece. Or completely terrible – as many, many critics have argued over the last week, without being fully free to say why. That is not their fault: media screenings around the world opened with a plea from Warner Bros to not spoil the film’s central reveal . This seems like it may have been a misstep, because curiosity and Cruise alone were clearly not enough to get bums on seats. Digger is now projected to lose around $150m , after taking a paltry $20m globally in its opening weekend. Warner Bros is trying to make the best of a bad situation, first crowing about the stinker reviews – “insufferable” and “smug” have been repeated a lot – then pivoting to a new sell: the Yanks don’t get it, so it must be good . Continue reading...

data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Poppy the curious, clever dog – who searches for missing people
data.description: A beloved family pet, she is also the best employee ever, brilliant at her rescue work. If everyone could be more like Poppy, the world would be a better place When we picked up a nine-week-old black labrador from a couple just outside Callander, Scotland, I had no idea that she would soon be an employee of mine. Poppy became the family fur baby and we realised early on how clever and empathic she is. I work as a Special Operations Response Team paramedic and we decided to involve her in my search work in 2021 when she was only a year old because we knew it would play to her strengths. She took to it immediately. Poppy and our team of dogs look for missing people. My colleagues and I then provide any medical assistance needed. She is trained to search without needing to smell someone’s scent from an item such as clothing. During training, we hide our volunteers along the riverbank, in the woods, beside lochs and canals, and set the dogs off. They have to find the people and come back. Poppy’s curious nature has served her well. She loves the undergrowth, sniffing about and finding things. Continue reading...

She is trained to search without needing to smell someone’s scent from an item such as clothing. During training, we hide our volunteers along the riverbank, in the woods, beside lochs and canals, and set the dogs off. They have to find the people and come back. Poppy’s curious nature has served her well. She loves the undergrowth, sniffing about and finding things. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘If it’s too slick, it looks like a fashion mag’: Peter Zumthor on his £110m rammed concrete gallery
data.description: It is one of the world’s finest collections, full of Monets, Miros and Picassos. But is the great Swiss architect’s extension for the Beyeler Foundation a worthy addition? Or is it a bit luxury boutique? In the early 1960s, when Peter Zumthor was a teenage apprentice in his father’s cabinet-making workshop, he designed his first cupboard. He later recalled the satisfaction of fitting the door so perfectly that it closed “with a special sucking sound”, saying his father instilled in him “the Basel pride in the well-built object” . Six decades on, with a fleet of globally celebrated projects to his name, the 83-year-old Swiss architect is back in Basel, beaming with the same local pride. He is gazing out at his latest well-built object, which is also his first project here: a monolithic new gallery that looks chiselled from the earth, its layers of pale crumbly concrete hammered into shape, its big oak and bronze doors – their handles wrapped with leather cord – closing with that same satisfyingly expensive Swiss swoosh. Continue reading...

data.title: Is your partner on their phone and ignoring you? I’ve got a buzzword for that
data.description: From microcheating to quiet quitting to weaponised incompetence, new terms to describe relationship failings are abundant. But that doesn’t mean there’s not space for some more ... Are you committing “attention infidelity”? The New York Times alerted me to this expression, coined by the public opinion researcher Daniel Cox in a new book on the “crisis of human connection”. It’s exactly what you’d expect: failing to focus fully on your partner because you’re indulging in what the NYT calls, rather judgily, “the banal distraction of dead-eyed scrolling”. Who are you calling dead-eyed? This reel of an armadillo in a paddling pool has my animated attention! Surely we’re all a bit attention-unfaithful – only saints don’t sometimes absent-mindedly thumb through medieval manuscript hedgehog memes while their partner relates a boring anecdote about how they thought they saw a strange bird that turned out to be a plastic bag. What I find more interesting is how we seem now to need a lexicon of relationship bad behaviour. Continue reading...

data.title: Social care for disabled adults is in as much crisis as support for elderly people – so why is the government silent about it? | John Harris
data.description: Working-age adults such as my son, who is autistic, face a fragmented and unreliable system, yet ministers talk only of a national care service for older people Seemingly brilliant conference speeches are often followed by a hangover, and so it has arguably proved with Andy Burnham’s. It was, it has to be said, something of a triumph, but there is now a familiar sense of nagging angst over how his big idea of a national care service is actually going to work. But equally, it doesn’t seem unreasonable to be more generous and patient. The policy issues are vast. The new PM’s commitment to serious change is clear. And having been urgently needed for years, the basics of what he wants – personal, home-based care delivered free at the proverbial point of need – will be on their way if Labour wins the next election. Here, though, is a question that is much less finely balanced. Neither Burnham’s speech nor the much shorter address given by Yvette Cooper , the new health and social care secretary, contained a single mention of what roughly half of England’s social care budgets are spent on: provision for working-age disabled adults. Why not? I get the politics: fixating on older people’s care and the pensions triple lock makes everything clear and relatable. But England’s fragmented, unreliable system for younger disabled adults is in need of the same radical level of reform, and it’s the source of just as much fear and worry for the people who either depend on it, or eventually will do. John Harris is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Trump’s recent statements on the economy are even more bonkers than usual | Steven Greenhouse
data.description: Our ‘genius’ president is revealing his ignorance of economics, fueling concerns about the threat he poses to the world Donald Trump recently made a bold claim about his abilities, writing on Truth Social : “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” But in the days before and after that post, Trump made one mind-boggling statement after another, including one that raised the possibility of cutting off all trade with dozens of the US’s trading partners. The president’s statements had many experts questioning not just his intelligence, but also whether he – and the outlandish policies he was proposing – were a clear and present danger to both the US economy and the world economy. Public respect for Trump’s economic sense has fallen so low that just 7% of Americans think he should take the lead in regulating AI, according to a recent WSJ poll . Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on trapped leaseholders: Labour must keep its promise to set them free | Editorial
data.description: The government pledged to end an unfair system. Ministers must give homeowners power over costs, rather than another place to complain “To the millions of leaseholders across the country, you have my word. The days of you being squeezed for every penny are coming to an end,” Andy Burnham told the Labour party conference . Only a few hours earlier, his housing secretary, Angela Rayner, had announced that the government would legislate for a new independent regulator and launch a consultation to cap “rip off” administrative fees. While these are undoubtedly steps in the right direction, they are miles away from Labour’s manifesto promise to “finally bring the feudal leasehold system to an end”. In its modern form , leasehold in England and Wales turns homes into income streams for freeholders. It should be abolished. There are powerful vested interests – billionaires , aristocrats and big businesses – that would oppose this move. But the system of service charges is crippling the housing market because its exorbitant cost puts off prospective buyers. The average annual service charge for a flat in England and Wales is now £2,405 , up 32.6% since 2020 and 55.6% over a decade. Owners of flats in high-rise blocks in London are paying service charges of more than £7,000 a year. Little wonder that first-time buyers are increasingly bypassing flats . Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on nurseries: some things are going right for under-fives | Editorial
data.description: England’s strong results in an early learning study are a Sure Start legacy that ministers must build on Recognition of the importance of babyhood and early childhood continues to grow. It is widely understood by many ordinary people, as well as experts, that what happens to us when we are very small, and our brains are at their most malleable , has lasting effects. As the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) put it in a study of early years education , “the first five years of a child’s life represent a window of opportunity, but also of vulnerability”. New Labour’s grasp of this underpinned its pioneering Sure Start programme. Much of this was dismantled under the Tory-Liberal Democrat austerity programme. But despite that loss, England’s results in this year’s OECD Early Learning and Child Well‑being Study were strong. This study does not have the high profile of the programme for international student assessment (Pisa) comparing the academic performance of 15-year-olds. It is newer and relies on a far smaller sample size. But while its findings should not be treated as gospel, it is heartening that England’s five-year‑olds were found to be thriving. On a social-emotional development measure, they came out on top. Continue reading...

data.title: Czechia’s Santi Denia: ‘Anthony Gordon? What a player! He’s at the same level as Lamine Yamal’
data.description: After working with nearly all of Spain’s World Cup-winning squad in their formative years, the coach is also a huge fan of English football. He’s now pitting his wits against both At the end of a 2-0 defeat by England in Prague, the Czechia coach turned left, walked along the touchline, shook Thomas Tuchel’s hand and said something he thinks he had never said at full-time: “See you soon.” To which Tuchel said back: “See you soon.” Seven days later, via Oviedo and Rijeka respectively, they meet again, at Wembley. “Four matches in 11 days, no time to train, for anything; I haven’t heard a single national coach say they like the new setup,” Santi Denia says, but it’s not all bad and there’s a big smile too. This is the start of a new life, yet familiar faces await, warmth in every word. Very familiar faces. If Czechia’s opponents in this Nations League could not have been much worse, they could not have been much better either. In Oviedo, Denia’s team played his country, his players; in London, for the second time in a week, they play the nation he knows better than any other, more footballers he has seen grown up. Hello, again. Continue reading...

data.title: The terrifying, unbeaten Chiefs would like you to know your predictions were wrong
data.description: Kansas City beat the surprisingly feisty Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. They already look like a very real contender after a lost season in 2025 The rivalry between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Las Vegas Raiders goes back to the formation of the American Football League in 1960, when the Chiefs were the Dallas Texans, and the Raiders resided in Oakland. At no time in that rivalry had both teams faced each other with a record of 3-0 or better until Sunday’s game at Las Vegas’s Allegiant Stadium. An unbeaten record wasn’t entirely surprising for the Chiefs with Patrick Mahomes, but the Raiders? The team won only three games in the whole of last season, but this new Raiders team under Klint Kubiak presents all kinds of challenges for opponents. At first, it appeared that the Raiders might go on to their first 4-0 start to a season since 2002, when they made it all the way to the Super Bowl, where they were vivisected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their former head coach, Jon Gruden. Kubiak’s team held a 13-10 halftime lead on Sunday, and Kubiak told CBS’s Tracy Wolfson at the half that his team was going to win the game . Continue reading...

They already look like a very real contender after a lost season in 2025 The rivalry between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Las Vegas Raiders goes back to the formation of the American Football League in 1960, when the Chiefs were the Dallas Texans, and the Raiders resided in Oakland. At no time in that rivalry had both teams faced each other with a record of 3-0 or better until Sunday’s game at Las Vegas’s Allegiant Stadium. An unbeaten record wasn’t entirely surprising for the Chiefs with Patrick Mahomes, but the Raiders? The team won only three games in the whole of last season, but this new Raiders team under Klint Kubiak presents all kinds of challenges for opponents. At first, it appeared that the Raiders might go on to their first 4-0 start to a season since 2002, when they made it all the way to the Super Bowl, where they were vivisected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their former head coach, Jon Gruden. Kubiak’s team held a 13-10 halftime lead on Sunday, and Kubiak told CBS’s Tracy Wolfson at the half that his team was going to win the game . Continue reading...

data.title: Djokovic rolls back years to beat Zverev as Sabalenka swept out in China Open
data.description: Novak Djokovic into semi-finals after 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 win Aryna Sabalenka loses to 34th-ranked Bartunkova Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a semi-final with Daniil Medvedev. The 39-year-old electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches. Djokovic got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly. Continue reading...

data.title: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support
data.description: Attack shortly after Friedrich Merz arrived on unannounced visit intended to underline Germany’s backing Russia has struck another major bridge in Kyiv as the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, arrived in the capital in a show of support for Ukraine. A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s key Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, marking the fourth consecutive day that Russia has targeted bridges used by tens of thousands of residents commuting between the city’s two banks. Video footage showed cars driving across the bridge as the drone plunged into the roadway and exploded in a burst of fire. Two people were injured in the strike, said Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Defend our men!’: fears for women’s rights in Latin America over plans to counter gender violence laws
data.description: Women ‘set back by 50 years’ as Bolivia, Chile, Argentina and Peru debate tougher penalties for false reports of sexual assaults, despite such cases being rare The Chilean senator Vanessa Kaiser is on a mission. In her view, men are under attack and need to be protected from the wrongs that feminism has brought about, including a barrage of false accusations of gender-based and sexual violence. “I want to be the first minister in the history of the west to defend men,” she says. “I want to defend you against the idea that, simply for being born male, you are guilty,” she said in July, speaking about a proposed bill that would create sanctions for falsely reporting domestic violence and sexual assaults. “Because now, on top of all the burdens we already had, thanks to those horrible ideologies called feminism and the gender perspective, we have to defend our men.” Continue reading...

data.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California
data.description: Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfires The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk. Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The future is bright’: breeding programme brings world’s heaviest insect back from the brink
data.description: Wētāpunga can weigh as much as a mouse and its numbers dwindled across New Zealand due to predators and habitat loss The population of New Zealand’s endemic wētāpunga – believed to be the world’s heaviest insect – is officially “recovering” thanks to a groundbreaking breeding programme that has overseen the release of 11,000 insects into the wild. “The future of wētāpunga is looking bright,” said Dr Chris Green, an honorary researcher at the department of conservation, who documented the success of the project for the New Zealand Journal of Zoology. Green co-authored a report released on 2 October that outlines the success of the breeding programme. Continue reading...

data.title: British government ‘complacent about food as a national security matter’
data.description: Experts say country does not have plan to feed people in a crisis and is unprepared for future shortages Britain does not have a plan for how to feed people in a crisis and is unprepared for potential future food shortages, according to a warning from more than 150 experts delivered to Andy Burnham. The climate crisis, geopolitical shocks, cyber-attacks and energy outages are among the threats to food chain security, according to the open letter, which claims the government is “complacent about food as a national security matter”. Establish a new system of local food resilience committees under the Civil Contingencies Act 2004. Audit the UK’s reliance on a few very large food companies and food imports. Realign national food production around nutritional needs. Create national, regional, local and community food storage schemes. Support the decentralisation of the UK’s food supply. Continue reading...

data.title: Shortages of crucial HIV medicines due to aid cuts are a ‘warning’, say experts
data.description: More than half of organisations providing HIV care surveyed by International Planned Parenthood Federation said they had run out of stock at some point during past 12 months Aid cuts have affected HIV drug and test supplies across the world, with some providers reporting they are out of stock of key medicines, according to a survey of 40 countries. Organisations providing HIV care revealed that more than half (55%) had run out of stock within the past year, with a critical scarcity of HIV tests and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) – a prescription medicine that people take to reduce the risk of getting HIV. data.title: Forty years of the Phantom of the Opera - the show that wouldn’t die: ‘People come back to hear the impossible’
data.description: As Andrew Lloyd Webber’s enduring gothic melodrama celebrates its 40th birthday, producer Cameron Mackintosh and cast members from down the years recall what makes it so special There is something about Andrew Lloyd Webber’s masterly musical The Phantom of the Opera – celebrating 40 years on the West End this month – which seems to take hold of its fans in a special way. For me, it was the show that first sparked my love of theatre and inspired me to work in the industry. Even today, Phantom is still the memory that gets my heart racing as I sit in the stalls, waiting impatiently for the curtain to come up, hoping for an experience just as intoxicating and all-consuming as that very first experience all those years ago. It’s not just the fans, either. When I talk to a cluster of key creatives, all of whom have a special working relationship with the show, each of them seems a little spellbound by Phantom. Sierra Boggess, who plays Carlotta in the 40th-anniversary production, talks tearfully about the lingering spirits of original director Hal Prince and choreographer Gillian Lynne. Jordan Donica, now starring as the Phantom in the West End, speaks passionately about the power of Lloyd Webber’s music (“It feels like heaven to me”), and John Owen-Jones, who has played the Phantom more than anyone else in the West End, talks tenderly about his long-term history with the show: “I’ve got a picture of me in full Phantom get-up holding my baby daughter. It’s an incredible thing to be part of.” Continue reading...

data.title: The Yellow Tie review – John Malkovich gives major hauteur as legendary record-hating maestro
data.description: This biopic of Sergiu Celibidache, the renowned Romanian conductor who refused all recordings, is a sturdy labour of love directed by his son Here is an old-fashioned biopic from central Europe that is also a labour of love on the part of its director: a little stolid and stately, yes, but robustly made, heartfelt and high-minded, with workmanlike performances and decent visual effects work. It is the story of the Romanian conductor and composer Sergiu Celibidache, a brilliant musician who became renowned among musical connoisseurs in the years following the second world war for his unique and uncompromisingly purist belief – derived from his Zen Buddhist studies – that music should never be recorded. He believed that LPs and CDs were inert and dead, and that music had to be experienced live, in the passionately authentic present. The director is the musician’s son, Serge Ioan Celebidachi, and as an older man in his rural French retirement, he is played with unsubtly querulous hauteur by John Malkovich, especially in the misjudged opening scene where he yells at Japanese executives for presuming to offer him a recording deal. Ben Schnetzer is the younger Celibidache, a prodigy whose musical ambition infuriates his old-fashioned father (Sean Bean), a well-regarded functionary who assumed that his son would follow him into public office. Celebidache Sr therefore demands the return of his birthday gift, a certain type of yellow tie that had been favoured by generations of the family’s menfolk, and which here becomes a fetish of the heartbroken young Sergiu’s need to please his father but also break away from him. Continue reading...

data.title: Karl review – straightforward tribute tells inside story of fashion world’s great eccentric Karl Lagerfeld
data.description: Based on Lagerfeld’s biography, director Nick Hooker gets access to the designer’s inner circle, but ultimately fails to find the man behind the high collar and sunglasses Karl Lagerfeld had never set foot inside a supermarket before he had one built on a catwalk in 2014, featuring models browsing aisles with baskets shopping for Chanel-branded fromage. It was classic Lagerfeld: very silly but a stroke of genius. The fashion designer was easy to poke fun at, with his white bouffant-plus-ponytail hairstyle and black leather gloves. But behind the persona was a man who spoke four languages fluently, a workaholic still running Chanel, Fendi and his own label Karl Lagerfeld into his 80s. This dutiful, uncontroversial documentary is based on William Middleton’s biography Paradise Now: The Extraordinary Life of Karl Lagerfeld . As well as archive footage of Lagerfeld, film-maker Nick Hooker gets access to the designer’s inner circle, but ultimately his documentary fails to chip away at the persona. (This is no criticism: I once interviewed Lagerfeld, a frustrating 30 minutes during which the dark glasses stayed on and he answered questions with bon mot witticisms but gave nothing away.) But behind the persona was a man who spoke four languages fluently, a workaholic still running Chanel, Fendi and his own label Karl Lagerfeld into his 80s. data.title: Charlie Shaw’s Revenge review – creepy clown killer takes aim at struggling amusement park
data.description: Decent effects and a late-stage twist show promise, but this gore-fest needs to be more disgusting, funny or unnerving The film opens with a lone figure striding into the foreground. He’s an amateur entertainer on his way to a gig, and he’s not been met at the station as planned. Still, not to worry – a car pulls up, and he gets in. But needless to say, his days (indeed, his minutes) are numbered. The murder that goes down in short order features plenty of blood but somehow fails to terrify the viewer. This is a problem unfortunately not limited to the opening scene: despite the various gruesome killings on show, there’s not much in the way of scares. The plot involves an adventure park in danger of going out of business, with the band of workers trying to get the place back on track providing plenty of fodder for a killer who spends some of the time dressed as a creepy clown. It’s easy to be dismissive of demon-clown films like Terrifier but they are effective in what they seek to do. Charlie Shaw’s Revenge isn’t – partly because the performances generally land some distance short of plausible, and partly because the writing itself is painfully thin. (The effects work, on the other hand, is decent, and the use of real locations with real animals is very welcome in a film-making era of green screen and expensive but hastily cobbled together CGI.) Continue reading...

data.title: TV tonight: an essential film about the story of Damilola Taylor
data.description: John Boyega, who was friends with Damilola, speaks in this moving programme. Plus: David Harewood’s superb new legal drama. Here’s what to watch this evening 9pm, BBC Two It’s been 26 years since 10-year-old Damilola Taylor was killed by teenagers. For the first time, the last people to see him alive create this essential account: from the actor John Boyega and Boyega’s sister Grace (Damilola’s mates who were at the library with him) to Guillermo Casal (the North Peckham Estate caretaker who found Damilola and cradled him as he died). His brother Tunde and the former Met officer Leroy Logan also revisit events, which eventually led to the conviction of two brothers, and take a wider look at why there were so many similar killings. The trauma and sadness remain palpable, but there is also a lot of love and even hope to be found in Damilola’s legacy. Hollie Richardson Continue reading...

data.title: Sleeping Beauties by David Byrne review – a quirky journey through the afterlife of invention
data.description: The Talking Heads frontman considers the dormant ideas that made a comeback – from Indian irrigation to Kafka There’s barely been a moment in  the last half-century when David Byrne hasn’t been zinging about, dancing forward, opting odd. The art-school dropout frontman of Talking Heads, he moved sideways into ballet, dance and experimental theatre, collaborated on the proto-ambient LP My Life in the Bush of Ghosts with his fellow polymath Brian Eno, directed films, wrote musicals (on – of course – Imelda Marcos), co-founded a label (Luaka Bop) that introduced the likes of Os Mutantes and William Onyeabor to a new generation, brought out books of tree drawings, and designed bicycle racks. Byrne’s career – by most measures a remarkably successful one – has been built from code-switching, fidgety intelligence, stylistic infidelity. At first glance then, it’s surprising that Sleeping Beauties is devoted to failure – to artists who were ignored, laughed at, forgotten; to ideas deemed batty or heretical; to ways of thinking about the world – sustaining it, replenishing it – that, often for political reasons, were found wanting, and wiped from our collective memory banks. Sleeping beauties is (of course) a term he first encountered in an academic paper by Leiden University scientometrics professor Ton van Raan. That was in 2004: this book, like a lot of the ideas and energies it animates, needed time to ferment. Continue reading...

data.title: The Housekeeper by Rose Tremain review – a bloodless origin story for Du Maurier’s Rebecca
data.description: The novelist has expanded her devastating 2014 short story about an imagined affair between Daphne du Maurier and a fictional Polish-Jewish housekeeper The rollcall of notable novels that began life as short stories is surprisingly long and various. Two years before Clarissa Dalloway famously shopped for flowers in Virginia Woolf’s Mrs Dalloway she was shopping for gloves in Woolf’s short story Mrs Dalloway in Bond Street; Evan S Connell’s Mrs Bridge and Jeffrey Eugenides’s The Virgin Suicides began life as stories published in the Paris Review. Rachel Cusk’s story Project, which ran in the New Yorker in September 2025, serves almost word for word as the opening for her new novel, Life of M. The newest addition to that list is Rose Tremain’s 17th novel, The Housekeeper, which pays homage to Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca by imagining the events that might have inspired it. Tremain first explored the idea in a 2014 story, also called The Housekeeper and included in her acclaimed collection The American Lover . Her protagonist, then and now, is Lilianne Danowski, a Polish Jew who fled the pogroms with her father as a child and who presides with reserved efficiency over a large staff at Manderville Hall near Fowey in Cornwall. When Du Maurier comes to lunch, it is Danowski, known to her employers as Danni (Danowski was “a mouthful of fishbones”), who is deputised to show her around the house, who proudly encourages Du Maurier to look through the clothes in her dead mistress’s fastidiously maintained bedroom and takes her down to the boat house. It is Danowski who, after a passionate year-long affair with Du Maurier, will be twisted into the malevolent Mrs Danvers. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Each artist on their own terms’: why Lee Krasner was every bit the equal to husband Jackson Pollock
data.description: At a landmark exhibition at New York’s Met Museum, Mrs Pollock finally steps out of her spouse’s shadow In addition to managing her own career as an artist and being a devoted partner to an often unpredictable and tumultuous Jackson Pollock , Lee Krasner had at least one other duty – acting as the unofficial publicist to her husband’s career. “She was a great champion of Pollock’s work, but also so aware of the gender politics of the time,” says curator David Breslin, who alongside Brinda Kumar worked for three long years to bring a new blockbuster dual show , exploring the arc of Pollock’s and Krasner’s careers, to the public at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. “She was such a realist, she knew if there was one person in the couple who would sell, it was him. She wanted to pay the bills. Continue reading...

data.title: How to make the perfect zuppa di cozze – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …
data.description: A tomatoey, southern Italian alternative to moules marinière – but who makes the definitive version? Abundant, good value and ready in minutes, mussels are one of my favourite seafoods, but when it comes to preparing them, I rarely look farther than northern France. Italians, of course, also eat mussels, and this tomato-rich recipe is a particular favourite in the south – Neapolitans traditionally tuck into zuppa di cozze on Maundy Thursday but it’s found on menus all year round. With its bold flavours and oily, garlicky sauce, it’s a great alternative to creamy moules marinières , and similarly needs no accompaniment but a hunk of bread to make a meal, though chips, of course, are rarely unwelcome. data.title: Miu Miu turns ‘real clothes’ into high fashion with sportswear style
data.description: Brand’s signature desire to subvert the ordinary brings blazers with track pants and crop tops under blazers to Paris fashion week Speaking backstage at Miu Miu’s show on Sunday at Paris fashion week, Miuccia Prada said she had been thinking about “real clothes”. The clothes people wear on the street for running errands rather than posing on social media. Her findings? Succinct. “The reality of clothing today is this mix – sportswear, casual, normal,” she said. Her challenge? To make them “more interesting, more rich”. To achieve this, she outlined how she had decided to focus on mixing “elements of sports with sophistication”. The collection opened with a series of five neatly pleated checked skirts. The first was worn with an equally neat checked blazer but rather than a smart shoe, such as a pump or loafers, there were brightly coloured trainers. The second featured a crop top under the blazer, the trainers swapped for spiky high heels. The other looks ditched the blazer and clipped the tops so they sat just under the bust line. Continue reading...

data.title: Spain’s Sánchez calls snap election amid national housing crisis – Europe live
data.description: PM says vote will take place on 29 November after parliament rejected two of his government’s emergency relief measures The conservative People’s Party is very pleased with the announcement. “At last,” they say on their X, with a slick election video – set to the EU’s anthem “Ode to Joy” – to go along with it. Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap election for 29 November, just days after rightwing parties blocked his minority government’s emergency measures on housing amid widespread protests ( 9:10 ). The election will take place on Sunday, 29 November, the earliest possible date procedurally. In a fierce address, Sánchez framed the election as choice between “regressing” under a “far-right coalition” or “keeping moving forward” with his progressive administration ( 9:04 , 9:09 , 9:17 ). He said the election will be about who will guide Spain through a period of disruption amid high political tensions, global instability, climate emergency, and uncertainty posed by the rise of AI ( 9:13 ). data.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how quickly your brain is ageing; it effects memory, focus and mood
data.description: A groundbreaking study by UCLA Health highlights the intriguing link between gut bacteria and brain ageing in healthy adults. Analyzing brain scans and gut health of nearly 1,500 participants, researchers identified a correlation between the Brain Ageing Index and certain gut microbes. This suggests that optimizing gut health may be pivotal for preserving cognitive function and offers an early detection path for interventions aimed at promoting healthier brain ageing.

data.title: De kan ha löst universums stora gåta
data.description: Ett antal forskare har tillbringat år i en gammal guldgruva i South Dakota, en och en halv kilometer under jord. De vill hitta svaret på en av universums största gåtor – hur mörk materia egentligen ser ut. Länge har det varit känt att denna mystiska massa ständigt omger oss, och håller stjärnorna och galaxen på plats. Men mer har vi inte vetat, förrän nu. Forskarna tror sig nämligen vara på väg mot ett genombrott, som om det lyckas säkerligen skulle ge dem Nobelpriset.

data.title: ‘Telefoon en portemonnee inleveren’, zei de man in de metro
data.description: In de metro waarin Marcel van Roosmalen en zijn dochter (11) zaten, schreeuwde een man dat iedereen vijf minuten had om zijn telefoon en portemonnee bij hem in te leveren. De mensen keken de andere kant op en deden net alsof het niet gebeurde. Mijn  dochter had per ongeluk wel oogcontact gemaakt en kon daar niet meer mee stoppen omdat ze dacht dat hij ons nu in de gaten hield.

data.title: Marta Romanow: Inwestorzy szukają dziś nie tylko ulg, ale całego ekosystemu
data.description: Dla małych i średnich firm coraz ważniejsze jest to, czy mogą stać się częścią łańcucha dostaw dużego inwestora. Liczy się także dostęp do energii oraz infrastruktura i kompetencje kadr. data.title: Paweł Korzeniowski: Park technologiczny musi być czymś więcej niż biurem
data.description: Park technologiczny powinien być platformą dostępu do laboratoriów, kompetencji, kontaktów, kapitału i technologii. Jego największą wartością jest łączenie tych zasobów tak, aby przedsiębiorca mógł przejść drogę od pomysłu, przez badania i wdrożenie, aż po skalowanie produkcji – mówi Paweł Korzeniowski, wiceprezes Wrocławskiego Parku Technologicznego.

data.title: Rewolucja w Wojsku Polskim po 30 latach. MON prezentuje nowy mundur i kamuflaż
data.description: Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej zaprezentowało nowy wzór munduru polowego dla żołnierzy Wojska Polskiego. To pierwsza tak gruntowna zmiana umundurowania od ponad trzech dekad. Nowy komplet oferuje lżejsze i wytrzymalsze materiały, nowoczesny układ kamuflażu oraz – po raz pierwszy w historii – krój zaprojektowany z myślą o kobietach.

data.title: Výbuch auta u Tuly zlikvidoval ruského veterána. Kyjev ho vinil z mučení vězňů
data.description: Exploze výbušniny umístěné pod vozidlem zabila jeho řidiče v ruském městě Novomoskovsk v Tulské oblasti. Podle místních novin patřil vůz Romanu Syromjatnikovovi, bývalému vězeňskému dozorci, který se zúčastnil ruské invaze na Ukrajinu. Kyjev ho eviduje na seznamu obviněných z válečných zločinů včetně mučení vězňů.

data.title: Začal týden Nobelových cen. Pozornost poutá kategorie za mír, kvůli Trumpovi
data.description: Nejvyšším vyznamenáním na poli vědy a techniky, stejně jako v oblasti zásluh o rozvoj lidstva, je Nobelova cena udělovaná v celkem šesti kategoriích. Laureáty, jež vždy v říjnu vyhlašuje několik švédských a norských institucí, se vyjma věhlasu mohou těšit i na medaili, diplom a milionovou odměnu. Slavnostní předání ocenění každoročně připadá na prosinec.

data.title: Téměř stovka událostí za víkend. Hasiči v Pardubickém kraji zachraňovali i drůbež
data.description: Hasiči v Pardubickém kraji za víkend vyjížděli k 94 událostem. Podle tiskové mluvčí Lucie Pipiš je to v porovnání s předchozími měsíci neobvykle vysoký počet zásahů většího rozsahu. Několik příkladů? Na Chrudimsku přesouvali tisíce kuřat a krůt z haly zasažené požárem. V Cholticích na Pardubicku zase zachránili kočku ze zakouřeného domu. Nebo v Lázních Bohdaneč likvidovali požár karavanu a dalších vozidel.

data.title: Marvanová vypovídá v Dozimetru. Ocitla jsem se v mafii, šikanovali mě, popsala
data.description: V pondělí se k Obvodnímu soudu pro Prahu 9 vrátila kauza Dozimetr. Jako svědkyně vypovídá bývalá pražská radní a současná senátorka a zastupitelka Hana Kordová Marvanová. Ta v inkriminované době podle svých slov ještě jako členka hnutí STAN na podezřelé zakázky sama upozorňovala. U soudu popisuje spory s Petrem Hlubučkem i ostatními členy Rady hlavního města. V jednu chvíli měla prý pocit, že se ocitla v mafii.

data.title: Před lety skoro ubil přítelkyni. Teď stojí invalidní důchodce opět před soudem
data.description: Karel Sluka z Plzně, který v minulosti dostal deset let vězení za pokus o vraždu své bývalé přítelkyně, znovu stanul před soudem. Tentokrát státní zástupce viní sedmapadesátiletého muže z pokusu o těžké ublížení na zdraví. Podle spisu obžalovaný několikrát vystřelil plynovou pistolí na muže, s nímž měl dlouhodobé spory.

data.title: Cíl byl náraz do letiště, přiznal pilot. Plán by do poslední chvíle nikdo neodhalil
data.description: Kdyby se mu plán podařil, nikdo by si do posledních sekund ničeho nevšiml. Radikalizovaný pilot letu Flydubai podle vyšetřovatelů původně plánoval narazit do letiště Bena Guriona. Podezřelý útočník čeká v cele na zřejmě nejpřísnější trest. Vyšetřování otevírá bezpečnostní prověrky i stopy, které za sebou zanechal na univerzitách ve Velké Británii a Austrálii.

data.title: Pražané jsou nespokojení s řízením města. Problémová je i digitalizace
data.description: Pražané vystavili vedení hlavního města před komunálními volbami nepříliš lichotivé vysvědčení. Fungování metropole hodnotí v průměru známkou 3,4 a jen 13 procent obyvatel má pocit, že je dnes Praha řízena efektivněji než před několika lety. Výhrady přitom zaznívají i od potenciálních voličů Pirátů, kteří jsou součástí vedení Prahy od roku 2018 a v současné radě mají na starosti mimo jiné oblast ICT a digitalizace.

data.title: Ministerstvo znovu hledá šéfa Národní galerie. První tendr Klempíř zrušil
data.description: Ministerstvo kultury vyhlásilo nové výběrové řízení na generálního ředitele nebo ředitelku Národní galerie Praha. Přihlášky včetně koncepcí uchazečů na šest let přijímá do 5. listopadu. Hodnotit je bude komise složená z mezinárodních odborníků. Výběrové řízení je po odvolání bývalé ředitelky galerie Alicji Knastové letos druhé, první ministr kultury Oto Klempíř zrušil začátkem července.

data.title: Střet auta s motorkou nejhůře odnesla opodál stojící cyklistka, letěl pro ni vrtulník
data.description: Kuriózní incident se stal v neděli u obce Horní Újezd na Přerovsku. Řidička osobního auta nejprve na křižovatce - ač měla přednost - pustila zleva jedoucího motorkáře. Následně se do křižovatky rozjela, ovšem patrně přehlédla motorkářku, která následovala svého kolegu. Po střetu s autem narazil motocykl do opodál stojících cyklistů a cyklistek, jedna z nich musela být letecky transportována do nemocnice.

data.title: Estonsko přesouvá vojska k Rusku, aby mohlo udeřit v hloubi jeho území
data.description: Estonsko trvale přesouvá svá vojska blíž k hranici s Ruskem a pořizuje si zbraně, s nimiž bude moci zasáhnout cíle hluboko na ruském území, napsal list Financial Times (FT). Rusko se podle Estonců v příštích dvou letech nechystá rozpoutat otevřenou válku s NATO, varují však zároveň, že se Moskva připravuje na potenciální budoucí konflikt. O hrozbě střetu s Ruskem promluvil i šéf Spolkové zpravodajské služby (BND).

data.title: Macronova francouzská revoluce končí. Země se potýká s dluhy i slabým růstem
data.description: Když Emmanuel Macron před deseti lety vstupoval do francouzské politiky, sliboval ekonomickou a politickou revoluci. Chtěl z Francie udělat moderní, podnikatelsky přívětivou a proevropskou velmoc. Jeho éra ale končí ve znamení rostoucího dluhu, slabšího růstu a politické paralýzy. Investoři navíc začínají zemi vnímat jako nejslabší článek eurozóny.

data.title: Avengers už zase překonali Avatara. Film Endgame je nejvýdělečnějším vůbec
data.description: Vrátit do kin po sedmi letech někdejší druhý nejvýdělečnější film historie Avengers: Endgame s podtitulem Encore byl dobrý tah. Superhrdinský tým se už léta přetahuje s modrými Pandořany o první příčku v žebříčku nejvýdělečnějších filmů a Encore nalákal na přidané záběry tolik fanoušků, že se dostal na jedničku.

data.title: Nobelova cena za medicínu patří třem laureátům za objev optogenetiky

To se potvrdilo, když si letošní ocenění odnesla trojice laureátů Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann a Georg Nagel. data.title: Plicní mor: jaké jsou příznaky, jak se šíří a proč je nejnebezpečnější formou nemoci
data.description: Plicní mor patří k nejzávažnějším formám moru. Nemoc způsobuje bakterie Yersinia pestis a bez rychlé léčby může člověka během velmi krátké doby ohrozit život. Na rozdíl od nejčastějšího dýmějového moru se navíc může přenášet přímo mezi lidmi. Při včasném nasazení antibiotik je však léčitelný.

data.title: Španělský premiér Sánchez vyhlásil uprostřed protestů předčasné volby
data.description: Španělský premiér Pedro Sánchez vyhlásil předčasné volby. Budou se konat v neděli 29. listopadu. V krátkém prohlášení z vládního paláce Moncloa řekl, že chce rozšířit levicovou a progresivní koalici, která vládla ve Španělsku v posledních letech. Předčasné volby uvítala opoziční Lidová strana, která k nim už řadu měsíců vyzývala.

data.title: Vláda projednává změnu financování asistentů pedagoga v základních školách
data.description: Koaliční kabinet Andreje Babiše projednává změnu ve financování asistentů pedagoga v základních školách. Asistenti pedagoga by mohli být financováni ze státního rozpočtu podle počtu žáků ve třídách a potřeb dětí namísto podle doporučení pro konkrétního žáka jako nyní. Novelu předložil vládě ministr školství za ANO Robert Plaga.

data.title: Pražský zastupitel bydlí ve státním bytě za deset tisíc. Vlastní bydlení má poblíž
data.description: Dlouholetý zastupitel osmé městské části v Praze Tomáš Němeček, který kandiduje i v letošních komunálních volbách za hnutí Osmička žije & Praha sobě, již téměř deset let užívá státní byt v areálu Psychiatrické nemocnice v Bohnicích (PNB). Pro instituci ale již deset let interně nepracuje a společně s manželkou navíc zároveň vlastní byt v sousedních Kobylisích, kde má i trvalé bydliště. Advokátní kancelář, v níž Němeček působí, nicméně PNB dodává právní služby.

data.title: Coalition says 100 fighter jets took part in ‘Operation Dawn of Yemen’
data.description: RIYADH: The coalition fighting to restore legitimacy in Yemen said that 100 fighter jets took part in Monday's morning launch of “Operation Dawn of Yemen,” destroying 324 high-value targets. Coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki said their forces are providing air cover to secure the Bab Al-Mandab Strait, while operations against moving targets remain ongoing. The coalition also said it is providing round-the-clock air support to Yemeni armed forces operating on the ground.

data.title: Iraq approves $2.7bn financing package to stimulate economy
data.description: Iraq has approved a 3.5 trillion dinar ($2.7 billion) financing package directed by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to stimulate its economy. The package aims to finance projects, support real estate, industrial, and agricultural sectors, and settle dues owed to contractors and farmers. This initiative comes amidst significant economic pressures on Iraq, including disruptions to oil exports and declining government revenues.

data.title: Karina Gómez Franco: “No vamos a permitir que el cine venezolano se apague por pequeñas miserias”
data.description: Tras superar la cancelación provocada por episodios de censura y acciones judiciales, la presidenta del Festival del Cine Venezolano confirmó el regreso del certamen del 22 al 26 de noviembre en las salas de Cinex del centro comercial Parque Costazul, en Margarita. La gran fiesta del cine venezolano ofrecerá una edición doble —correspondiente a los años 2025 y 2026— que reunirá cerca de 80 largometrajes entre ficción y documental, además de cortometrajes y producciones de la categoría Universidad Audiovisual. Habrá homenajes para el fallecido empresario Alexis Montilla, de La Venezuela de Antier, y la productora Cinesa. The post Karina Gómez Franco: “No vamos a permitir que el cine venezolano se apague por pequeñas miserias” appeared first on EL NACIONAL .

data.title: Primus Ligue J5 : Le jour où Intwari a vu le ciel tomber sur Vital’O et Rukinzo déchaîner les enfers
data.description: Il y a des journées de championnat qui se contentent d'aligner des scores. Et puis, il y a celle-ci. data.title: FFB : Le Comité Exécutif passe au crible les grands chantiers du football burundais
data.description: Ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, le Comité Exécutif de la Fédération de Football du Burundi s'est réuni autour de son Président, le Général de Brigade de Police Alexandre Muyenge. Au menu des échanges : le bilan du match Burundi - Algérie comptant pour les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, les préparatifs du duel Burundi - Ouganda en éliminatoires de la CAN Beach Soccer 2026, l'état d'avancement de la préparation des U17 pour la CECAFA Rwanda 2026, ainsi que le suivi de la Primus Ligue 2026-2027.

data.title: La déroute abyssale de Vital’O FC au Stade Intwari
data.description: Il y a des jours où le football cesse d'être un jeu pour devenir une tragédie. Ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, au Stade Intwari, le choc tant annoncé de la cinquième journée de la Primus Ligue 2026-2027 n'a pas eu lieu. A sa place, il y a eu une exécution. Une symphonie en cinq actes jouée par Vision FC, et subie comme un calvaire par un Vital'O FC méconnaissable.

data.title: Higher diesel costs increase the electricity tariff
data.description: Nuku'alofa, Tonga PUBLIC NOTICE The Tonga Energy Commission has approved a revised electricity tariff of 115.49 seniti per kilowatt-hour for the October to December 2026 quarter, effective 1 October. This is an increase of 3.92 seniti, or 3.51% per cent, from the July to September tariff rate of 111.57 seniti. The tariff increase is mainly due to the higher approved price of diesel used to generate electricity. The October power-generation diesel price is 6.5 per cent higher than September, following an increase of nearly 10% per cent in September. Tonga’s heavy reliance on diesel generation means these increases raise the cost of supplying electricity. Conflict in the Middle East and disruption to fuel production and shipping have caused sharp movements in international diesel prices. Tonga depends on imported fuel and remains exposed to these changes. Rising local diesel prices increase the amount Tonga Power must pay for fuel to maintain electricity supply. The Commission recognises the pressure that higher electricity costs place on families and businesses. The Fuel/ RE Component increases from 65.89 to 69.81 seniti per kilowatt-hour, while the non-fuel component remains unchanged at 45.68 seniti. The adjustment allows Tonga Power to recover its permitted fuel and renewable energy costs. Fuel prices remain volatile. If diesel prices change sharply, electricity tariffs may need to be adjusted before the next quarterly reviser effect on the cost of electricity supply. Fuel & Renewable Cost Adjustments Mechanism for the Tonga Electricity Tariff Effective Oct 1, 2026, the revised power tariff will be $1.1549 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), reflecting a 3.51% increase from the previous months adjustment rate of $1.1157.  This increase is driven by a significant rise in the diesel fuel price for power generation for September and October 2026 compared to previous months. Meleseini Folau, Acting Chief Executive Officer -- FANONGONONGO Ko e hiki e totongi ʻo e tīsolo ʻoku ne fakatupu e hiki ʻa e totongi ʻuhilá Kuo tali ʻe he Komisoni ki he Maʻuʻanga Ivi ʻa Tongá ha totongi ʻuhila kuo fakaleleiʻi ko e seniti ʻe 115.49 ki he kilouati houa ʻe taha, ki he kuata ʻo ʻOkatopa ki Tīsema 2026. ʻE kamata ngāueʻaki ʻa e totongi foʻoú ʻi he ʻaho 1 ʻo ʻOkatopa. Ko ha hiki ʻeni ʻaki ʻa e seniti ʻe 3.92, pe ko e 3.51%, mei he totongi ʻo e kuata ʻo Siulai ki Sepitema, ko e seniti ʻe 111.57. Ko e tupu ʻa e totongi ʻuhilá ʻoku tupu lahi ia mei he hiki ʻa e totongi tīsolo kuo tali, ʻa ia ʻoku ngāueʻaki ki hono fakatupu ʻo e ʻuhilá. Ko e totongi tīsolo ki hono fakatupu ʻo e ʻuhilá ʻi ʻOkatopá ʻoku māʻolunga ʻaki ʻa e 6.5% ʻi he totongi ʻo Sepitemá, hili e tupu meimei 10% ʻi Sepitemá. Koeʻuhí ʻoku lahi ʻaupito ʻa e fakafalala ʻa Tonga ki hono fakatupu ʻo e ʻuhilá mei he tīsolo, ʻoku fakatupu ʻe he ngaahi hikihiki ko ʻení ʻa e tupu ʻa e fakamolé ki hono fakahoko ʻo e ʻuhilá. Kuo fakatupu ʻe he fepakipaki ʻi he Hahake Lotolotó mo e uesia ʻa hono ngaohi mo fetuku ʻo e lolo ha ngaahi liliu lahi ʻi he ngaahi totongi tīsolo fakavahaʻapuleʻangá. ʻOku fakafalala ʻa Tonga ki he lolo ʻoku hū mai mei muli, pea ʻoku uesia ai ʻe he ngaahi liliu ko ʻení. ʻI he tupu ʻa e totongi tīsolo fakalotofonuá, ʻoku toe lahi ange ai ʻa e paʻanga kuo pau ke totongi ʻe he Kautaha ‘Uhila ‘a Tonga ki he lolo ke fakapapauʻi ʻoku hokohoko atu ʻa e maʻu ʻuhilá. ʻOku ʻiloʻi ʻe he Komisoní ʻa e kavenga ʻoku fakatupu ʻe he totongi ʻuhila māʻolungá ki he ngaahi fāmili mo e ngaahi pisinisi. ʻOku hiki ʻa e konga ki he lolo/Maʻuʻanga Fakafou (Fuel/ RE Component) mei he seniti ʻe 65.89 ki he seniti ʻe 69.81ki he kilouati houa ʻe taha, kae kei tatau pē ʻa e konga ʻoku ʻikai kau ai ʻa e lolo, ko e seniti ʻe 45.68. ʻOku fakaʻatā ʻe he liliu ko ʻení ʻa e Kautaha Ma’u’anga Ivi ke toe maʻu ʻa e fakamole ki he lolo mo e maʻuʻanga ivi fakafoʻou kuo fakangofua. ʻOku kei fetōʻaki ʻa e ngaahi totongi lolo. Kapau ʻe liliu lahi ʻa e totongi tīsolo, ʻe ala fiemaʻu ke toe fakaleleiʻi ʻa e totongi ʻuhilá kimuʻa ʻi he to e vakaiʻi fakakuata hokó. Founga ki hono Fakaleleiʻi ʻo e Fakamole ki he Fefie mo e Maʻuʻanga Ivi Fakafoʻou ʻi he Totongi ʻUhila ʻa Tonga ʻI he kamataʻanga ʻo e ʻaho 1 ʻo ʻOkatopa 2026, ko e totongi ʻuhila foʻoú ko e seniti ʻe 115.49 ki he kilouati houa ʻe taha (kWh), ʻa ia ʻoku fakahaaʻi ai ha hiki ʻaki ʻa e 3.51% mei he totongi ki muʻa, ko e seniti ʻe 111.57. ʻOku tupu ʻa e hikí ni mei he lahi ʻa e tupu ʻa e totongi tīsolo ki hono fakatupu ʻo e ʻuhilá ʻi Sepitema mo ʻOkatopa 2026, ʻi hono fakahoa ki he ngaahi māhina kimuʻá.e Fetuʻutaki ki he Fanongonongo ni MeleseiniFolau, Pule Ngāue Pule Lahi Leʻoleʻo -- Sponsored Post #9536 promoted by Energy Commission of Tonga 5-12 October 2026 Pacific Islands Tonga Energy Commission electricity tariffs Sponsored Public Notice

Kuo fakatupu ʻe he fepakipaki ʻi he Hahake Lotolotó mo e uesia ʻa hono ngaohi mo fetuku ʻo e lolo ha ngaahi liliu lahi ʻi he ngaahi totongi tīsolo fakavahaʻapuleʻangá. ʻOku fakafalala ʻa Tonga ki he lolo ʻoku hū mai mei muli, pea ʻoku uesia ai ʻe he ngaahi liliu ko ʻení. ʻI he tupu ʻa e totongi tīsolo fakalotofonuá, ʻoku toe lahi ange ai ʻa e paʻanga kuo pau ke totongi ʻe he Kautaha ‘Uhila ‘a Tonga ki he lolo ke fakapapauʻi ʻoku hokohoko atu ʻa e maʻu ʻuhilá. ʻOku ʻiloʻi ʻe he Komisoní ʻa e kavenga ʻoku fakatupu ʻe he totongi ʻuhila māʻolungá ki he ngaahi fāmili mo e ngaahi pisinisi. ʻOku hiki ʻa e konga ki he lolo/Maʻuʻanga Fakafou (Fuel/ RE Component) mei he seniti ʻe 65.89 ki he seniti ʻe 69.81ki he kilouati houa ʻe taha, kae kei tatau pē ʻa e konga ʻoku ʻikai kau ai ʻa e lolo, ko e seniti ʻe 45.68. ʻOku fakaʻatā ʻe he liliu ko ʻení ʻa e Kautaha Ma’u’anga Ivi ke toe maʻu ʻa e fakamole ki he lolo mo e maʻuʻanga ivi fakafoʻou kuo fakangofua. ʻOku kei fetōʻaki ʻa e ngaahi totongi lolo. Kapau ʻe liliu lahi ʻa e totongi tīsolo, ʻe ala fiemaʻu ke toe fakaleleiʻi ʻa e totongi ʻuhilá kimuʻa ʻi he to e vakaiʻi fakakuata hokó. Founga ki hono Fakaleleiʻi ʻo e Fakamole ki he Fefie mo e Maʻuʻanga Ivi Fakafoʻou ʻi he Totongi ʻUhila ʻa Tonga ʻI he kamataʻanga ʻo e ʻaho 1 ʻo ʻOkatopa 2026, ko e totongi ʻuhila foʻoú ko e seniti ʻe 115.49 ki he kilouati houa ʻe taha (kWh), ʻa ia ʻoku fakahaaʻi ai ha hiki ʻaki ʻa e 3.51% mei he totongi ki muʻa, ko e seniti ʻe 111.57. ʻOku tupu ʻa e hikí ni mei he lahi ʻa e tupu ʻa e totongi tīsolo ki hono fakatupu ʻo e ʻuhilá ʻi Sepitema mo ʻOkatopa 2026, ʻi hono fakahoa ki he ngaahi māhina kimuʻá.e Fetuʻutaki ki he Fanongonongo ni MeleseiniFolau, Pule Ngāue Pule Lahi Leʻoleʻo -- Sponsored Post #9536 promoted by Energy Commission of Tonga 5-12 October 2026 Pacific Islands Tonga Energy Commission electricity tariffs Sponsored Public Notice

data.title: Kalev Mutond, ancien administrateur général de l’ANR, est mort à Paris
data.description: Kalev Mutond, ancien administrateur général de l’Agence nationale de renseignements (ANR), est décédé lundi 5 octobre à Paris en France, selon ses proches. Il était âgé de 69 ans. L’ancien responsable des renseignements congolais se trouvait dans la capitale française depuis près d’un an pour des soins médicaux, selon ses proches, qui n’ont pas communiqué les causes de son décès à ce stade.

data.description: Des dizaines d’enfants des localités de Kahunga et Karama, dans le groupement Bukoma, en territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu), abandonnent leur scolarité après la deuxième année primaire. data.title: Armwrestling: The 10-year journey of Ghana Armwrestling from a simple table to global glory
data.description:
Ten years ago, a dream was born around a simple wood-and-metal table. It was a vision to harness Ghanaian strength, courage and determination, give the sport a structured home and take it onto the world stage.

In 2016, Armwrestling formally entered Ghana’s national sports calendar when the Ghana Armwrestling Federation (GAF) earned official recognition as the country’s 40th national sporting federation. The Federation also secured affiliations with the Africa Armwrestling Federation (AFA) and the World Armwrestling Federation (WAF), laying the foundation for what would become a remarkable Ghanaian sporting story.

data.title: NPP is for all social classes, not just the middle class – Mike Oquaye
data.description:
Former Speaker of Parliament, Professor Mike Oquaye, has rejected suggestions that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) needs a leader specifically capable of winning back Ghana’s middle class.

He said the NPP should not be viewed as a party for only the middle class, saying that the party’s policies and social interventions have historically targeted people across different social groups.

Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Monday, October 5, Professor Oquaye was asked whether the NPP’s decision to elect John Boadu as chairman would help the party reconnect with the middle class.

The question followed arguments that the NPP had traditionally enjoyed stronger support among the middle class but lost some of that support after the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme, which critics said contributed to the party’s defeat in the 2024 general election.

data.title: John Boadu is ‘an exceptionally gifted political figure’ – Prof Mike Oquaye
data.description:
Former Speaker of Parliament, Professor Mike Oquaye, has described newly elected New Patriotic Party (NPP) Chairman John Boadu as an “exceptionally gifted political figure”, citing his long experience and rise through the ranks of the party.

Speaking in an interview on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Monday, October 5, Professor Oquaye said Mr Boadu’s knowledge of the NPP and his experience in different leadership positions made him well suited to lead the party as chairman.

When asked what he made of John Boadu’s election as chairman of the NPP, Professor Oquaye said Mr Boadu understood both the party’s history and the direction it needed to take.

data.title: NDC must study NPP congress closely for strategic lessons – Mustapha Gbande
data.description:
Deputy General Secretary in charge of Operations for Ghana's ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mustapha Gbande says the party must closely study the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) recent national delegates congress for strategic lessons ahead of the next phase of Ghana’s political contest.

Mr Gbande said the NDC, as the governing party and the traditional alternative to the NPP, has a responsibility to examine the outcome of the opposition party’s internal elections and assess its wider political implications.

Speaking about the NPP’s congress, he congratulated the party and its newly elected executives, describing the exercise as one of the more peaceful congresses the party has organised in recent times.

data.title: ‘Electing Kojo Bamba is backward politics’ – Mustapha Gbande
data.description:
Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mustapha Gbande, has criticised the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) election of Kojo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, as First Vice Chairman, describing the outcome as “backward politics.”

Speaking on JoyNews’ Joy AM, Mr Gbande argued that electing a former leader of a pro-NPP vigilante group to a senior party position projects a mindset of violence that, in his view, Ghana has moved beyond.

“To go and elect, projecting the mindset of violence, for me is backward politics. We have reserves for all of these,” he said.

Mr Gbande also rejected suggestions that the NPP’s new leadership could rely on violence or other means to influence future elections.

data.title: Manasseh Writes: The shift in the NPP
data.description:
Wars are fought and won with superior tactics and intellect, not with bigger muscles. Even in wrestling or boxing, when the size of muscles counts, the brain does not stop working.

To outwit your opponent in war, you need superior brainwork to craft superior strategies and invent weapons. So, even if violence is involved, intellect is still key.

Daring souls are needed to launch attacks, but without sharp minds at the table, daredevils only become casualties with no impact.

Political party leadership needs strategic thinkers. They mustn't appeal only to the party's hawks, who don't need any convincing to stay anyway. The average woman out there, even if not highly educated, would want to see leaders she could point to as role models for her children.

data.title: Dealing with political and social media insults
data.description:
If you are against social media insults, violent rhetoric and vulgar political speech, don’t play back, don’t watch the TikTok or YouTube videos, don’t re-broadcast or re-publish them on your social media accounts, blogs or media portals.

You all know that the more you engage with this violent and insulting content, the more social media platform algorithms show them to more people and the more those behind such despicable content become popular and are able to monetise their social media accounts. Don’t give oxygen to the fire and turn around to complain about public insults.

data.title: Bawumia unveils NPP plan to scout parliamentary candidates capable of winning parliamentary seats
data.description:
The presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has disclosed that the party has begun scouting for potential parliamentary candidates across constituencies ahead of the 2028 general elections.

He said the initiative is intended to identify candidates with the potential to win parliamentary seats, rather than relying solely on the outcome of internal primaries.

According to Dr Bawumia, some aspirants may have the financial resources to win an NPP parliamentary primary but may not necessarily be capable of winning the subsequent general election.

“We are going to do a candidate search across all the constituencies, because some people can win parliamentary primaries because they have money, but they can’t win the general elections,” he said.

He explained that allowing such candidates to emerge solely through the primary process could result in the party losing seats in the general election.

data.title: NPP Chairmanship race: How APL’s survey made a near-perfect prediction
data.description:
When the Electoral Commission declared John Boadu as NPP National Chairman-elect at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, political pollsters took notice for another reason - the accuracy of the survey conducted by policy think tank Africa Policy Lens (APL).

The APL had conducted a series of polls on the election, but 24 hours before delegates converged in Kumasi, the APL released its final poll projecting the outcome of a highly competitive chairmanship race. And when the ballot boxes were opened, its prediction turned out to be almost perfect.

data.title: ¿Mercado en el socialismo cubano: Adiós a la planificación?
data.description: Cuadrando la Caja aborda la relación entre planificación y mercado en el socialismo cubano ante las transformaciones económicas en curso. Los especialistas coinciden en que el mercado no es ajeno al socialismo y debe ganar peso en la asignación de recursos, pero regulado y subordinado al interés social. El reto es evitar desigualdades y mercantilización, fortaleciendo la planificación estratégica y la protección del pueblo. The post ¿Mercado en el socialismo cubano: Adiós a la planificación? first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Costa Rica se salva y el Caribe domina: así quedó el Grupo A de la Nations League
data.description: El Grupo A de la Liga de Naciones de Concacaf llegó a su cierre con una jornada cargada de emociones y con un claro protagonismo de las selecciones del Caribe . Curazao terminó como líder, Haití confirmó su gran campaña y Costa Rica logró salvarse del descenso después de un complicado inicio de torneo. Costa Rica llegó a la última jornada obligada a conseguir un buen resultado y respondió con una victoria 2-0 sobre Haití . Carlos Mora y Andrey Soto marcaron los goles que le permitieron a la selección costarricense sumar tres puntos fundamentales y asegurar su permanencia en la máxima categoría y quedó en la cuarta posición. Los ticos habían comenzado la competencia con una dolorosa derrota 4-3 ante Curazao y posteriormente cayeron 2-0 frente a Haití , quedando al borde del descenso. Sin embargo, reaccionaron con una victoria 3-0 ante Nicaragua y posteriormente derrotaron a Haití para completar la remontada. Mientras tanto, Curazao terminó en lo más alto del grupo . La selección caribeña cerró su participación con un empate 1-1 ante Trinidad y Tobago , resultado que le permitió mantenerse en la cima después de una campaña sobresaliente. Jordi Paulina marcó para Curazao , mientras Luke Phillip había adelantado a Trinidad y Tobago. Reddit Curazao fue una de las grandes revelaciones de esta fase. En su debut protagonizó una espectacular remontada para vencer 4-3 a Costa Rica , luego goleó 6-1 a Nicaragua y consiguió otros resultados importantes que le permitieron mantenerse en la parte alta de la clasificación. Haití también fue protagonista. Los caribeños llegaron a la última jornada con posibilidades de terminar en lo más alto después de sumar victorias ante Trinidad y Tobago , Costa Rica y República Dominicana. Sin embargo, la derrota 2-0 ante los ticos los dejó por debajo de Curazao . La otra cara de la moneda fue Nicaragua . La selección centroamericana no pudo reaccionar durante la fase de grupos y terminó en el último lugar, por lo que quedó condenada al descenso a la Liga B . Los nicas cayeron de nuevo en casa contra República Dominicana 1-2 en el último partido del grupo. Los dominicanos fueron la gran sorpresa y por diferencia de goles no clasificaron a la siguiente ronda. El Grupo A dejó, además, una conclusión importante: el Caribe fue el gran protagonista . Curazao y Haití terminaron demostrando un crecimiento importante y se metieron entre los equipos que marcaron el paso durante la competencia. ¿Qué pasa con la Copa Oro? La Nations League 2026-27 también es parte del camino clasificatorio hacia la Copa Oro 2027 . Concacaf estableció que los dos primeros lugares de cada grupo de la Liga A avanzan a los cuartos de final, mientras que los equipos que terminan tercero y cuarto deberán disputar las preliminares de la Copa Oro. Concacaf+1 En cuanto al descenso, Concacaf determinó que los equipos que terminen quinto y sexto de cada grupo de la Liga A bajarán a la Liga B . Concacaf Así quedó el Grupo A 1. Curazao — 10 puntos 2. Haití — 9 puntos 3.  República Dominicana — 9 puntos 4. Costa Rica — 6 puntos 5. Trinidad y Tobago — 2 puntos 6. Nicaragua — 0 puntos

data.title: Hondureño es acusado de atropellar y matar a una mujer en Indiana; andaba drogado
data.description: Indiana, Estados Unidos . Un hondureño de 22 años es acusado de atropellar y causar la muerte de Tamara Renee Thomas , de 33 años,  en el estacionamiento de una gasolinera en Indianápolis, Indiana, mientras presuntamente conducía intoxicado. El vehículo era conducido presuntamente por el hondureño Edwin Alexander Sosa-Gonzalez , de 22 años. Según la investigación, Edwin Alexander Sosa conducía una Honda CR-V que previamente habría chocado contra otro vehículo antes de ingresar al estacionamiento de la gasolinera donde se encontraba Tamara. Las cámaras de seguridad habrían registrado el momento en que la mujer intentó correr para ponerse a salvo al observar que la camioneta se aproximaba. Sin embargo, fue alcanzada por el vehículo y declarada fallecida en el lugar. Tras el impacto, el hondureño presuntamente abandonó la camioneta y escapó a pie. De acuerdo con documentos judiciales, posteriormente habría contactado al propietario del vehículo para pedirle que lo reportara como robado. Horas después, la Policía logró localizar al hondureño. Las autoridades reportaron que presentaba señales de intoxicación al momento de ser ubicado. De acuerdo con los registros del caso, una prueba habría establecido un nivel de alcohol en sangre de 0.229. Esta cifra se encuentra por encima del límite legal de 0.08 establecido en Indiana para conducir. El hondureño fue acusado formalmente el 30 de septiembre por varios delitos, entre ellos causar una muerte mientras conducía intoxicado y abandonar la escena de un accidente fatal. data.translatedDescription: Indiana, Estados Unidos . Un hondureño de 22 años es acusado de atropellar y causar la muerte de Tamara Renee Thomas , de 33 años,  en el estacionamiento de una gasolinera en Indianápolis, Indiana, mientras presuntamente conducía intoxicado. El vehículo era conducido presuntamente por el hondureño Edwin Alexander Sosa-Gonzalez , de 22 años. Según la investigación, Edwin Alexander Sosa conducía una Honda CR-V que previamente habría chocado contra otro vehículo antes de ingresar al estacionamiento de la gasolinera donde se encontraba Tamara. Las cámaras de seguridad habrían registrado el momento en que la mujer intentó correr para ponerse a salvo al observar que la camioneta se aproximaba. Sin embargo, fue alcanzada por el vehículo y declarada fallecida en el lugar. Tras el impacto, el hondureño presuntamente abandonó la camioneta y escapó a pie. De acuerdo con documentos judiciales, posteriormente habría contactado al propietario del vehículo para pedirle que lo reportara como robado. Horas después, la Policía logró localizar al hondureño. Las autoridades reportaron que presentaba señales de intoxicación al momento de ser ubicado. De acuerdo con los registros del caso, una prueba habría establecido un nivel de alcohol en sangre de 0.229. Esta cifra se encuentra por encima del límite legal de 0.08 establecido en Indiana para conducir.
