data.title: Romania starts mobilization exercise for reservists in Bucharest, Ilfov
data.description: Romania’s Defense Ministry kicked off the  “MOBEX Bucharest - Ilfov 26” mobilization exercise on Monday, October 5, calling some 10,000 army reservists in the region to military units for one day of training. The reservists being called up are between 43 and 63 years old. According to the Ministry of National Defence, they are required to participate in training sessions and exercises to assess the reserve. The reservists concerned must report to the designated units only on the date indicated in the call-up order. The exercise, which will last until October 12, is routine. Employers must ensure the attendance of employed reservists at these activities by granting them one additional paid day of leave, based on the certificate issued by the military center. MOBEX-type exercises are planned and organized every year and generally target up to ten counties, the Ministry of National Defence said. The exercise also evaluates how structures with responsibilities in the field of national defence and security are staffed with human and material resources. “The training involves checking attendance, whether the uniforms and weapons are in order, as well as medical, communications and engineering training, firing the weapons provided, and presenting the equipment used by the units,” said Maj. Gen. Mircea Gologan, commander of MOBEX Bucharest-Ilfov 2026, cited by Libertatea . Before participating in the actual exercises, reservists must pass two essential tests: a medical one and a psychological one. A new element of this exercise is the use of a 9 mm pistol, recently integrated into the military equipment of the Bucharest Garrison. “As a unit element, we will conduct firing with the 9 mm pistol, newly introduced into service, also as a new element for the Bucharest Garrison. Most of them will be informed about the staff elements,” Col. Mihai Băltățescu, director of MOBEX Bucharest-Ilfov 2026, said. According to data from previous years, 8% of the reservists called up did not attend the mobilization exercises. Unjustified absence or refusal to receive the call-up order is considered a contravention and may be sanctioned with a fine. The last mobilization exercise in Bucharest and Ilfov County took place last year. To reduce the socioeconomic impact, it included only some of the military units deployed in the area. This year, the units that were not included in the “MOBEX B-IF-25” exercise will be assessed. “To avoid disinformation and fake news that could be spread in connection with these activities, we reiterate that such exercises are routine in nature and recommend that citizens obtain information from official sources,” the Ministry of National Defence said. As in the past, misinformation spread online regarding the exercise, with far-right social media influencers claiming it is connected to a supposed involvement by Romania in the war in Ukraine. Such claims have circulated since the start of the war in 2022, without any proof.

data.title: Chinese car brand LEPAS enters Romania, plans 24 dealerships by 2027
data.description: Chinese automotive brand LEPAS entered Romania with the opening of its first showroom in Sibiu and the launch of the L8 plug-in hybrid SUV. Materom, its exclusive Romanian importer, plans to expand the network to 12 dealerships by the end of 2026 and 24 in 2027. The brand currently has eight authorised dealers in Bacău, Brașov, Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Iași, Pitești, Sibiu, and Timișoara. Its planned network would cover around 80% of Romania’s main urban centres. “Romania is an important market in LEPAS’s European development strategy,” said Hedy Yan, Country Director of LEPAS Romania. “The opening of our first showroom in Sibiu and the launch of the L8 mark the beginning of this long-term commitment." The L8 is the first LEPAS model available locally. It combines a 1.5-litre petrol engine with an electric propulsion system and has a claimed combined range of up to 1,040 kilometres. According to manufacturer figures based on the WLTP testing procedure, combined fuel consumption is two litres per 100 kilometres. Consumption rises to six litres per 100 kilometres when the battery is depleted. The SUV is sold in Essence and Elegance versions. Its announced price is EUR 45,500, including VAT, while a launch discount temporarily lowers it to EUR 42,500. LEPAS plans to follow the L8 with the smaller L6, which will be offered in plug-in hybrid and fully electric versions. The model is due to be presented at the Bucharest Auto Show. The company is also preparing an L4 in both powertrain configurations, followed by two additional models scheduled for the third quarter of 2027. LEPAS said it had received almost 2,000 enquiries from potential Romanian customers ahead of the rollout. Materom operates a central spare-parts warehouse in Târgu Mureș and will oversee the local sales and servicing network. LEPAS is part of Chinese automaker Chery Group. Materom is a Romanian family-owned automotive group active in parts distribution, dealerships and vehicle servicing, with more than 25 years of experience.

data.title: PwC: Romania’s M&A market reaches EUR 2.3 bln in third quarter
data.description: Romania’s mergers and acquisitions market reached an estimated EUR 2.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026, 2.2 times the value recorded in the same period last year, according to PwC. A total of 93 transactions were announced, representing a 52% annual increase. The market value includes the acquisition of Electronic Arts by a consortium comprising the Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners. The share attributed to the video game company’s Romanian operations is estimated at more than EUR 650 million. Excluding the Electronic Arts deal, the average transaction value remained at approximately EUR 16 million, similar to the third quarter of 2025. “The deals market in the third quarter of 2026, in terms of both value and number of transactions, points to sustained investor interest in Romanian businesses,” said George Ureche, deals partner at PwC Romania. According to him, early results from the fiscal consolidation package, Romania’s continued investment-grade rating, and the prospect of joining the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development had supported market activity. Consolidation opportunities are being pursued mainly by strategic investors already active in Romania, he added. Excluding Electronic Arts, industrial products and services generated the largest share of transaction value, at approximately EUR 463 million, or 32% of the quarterly total. Energy followed with around EUR 232 million, representing 16%. Among the largest deals announced during the quarter were Scatec’s acquisition of the 77 MW Urleasca wind project, Apollo Global Management’s takeover of FORVIA’s interiors division, and Alimentation Couche-Tard’s acquisition of Żabka Group, including its Froo operations in Romania. Each was estimated at more than EUR 90 million. Other notable transactions included BasePoint Capital’s acquisition of International Personal Finance, whose Romanian operations are conducted through Provident Financial Romania, and an affiliate of Lone Star Funds’ acquisition of Continental’s ContiTech industrial division. According to the PwC report, only 11 of the 93 announced transactions exceeded EUR 40 million, indicating that Romania’s market remained dominated by smaller deals in numerical terms. Transactions involving European or international groups with Romanian operations generated EUR 1.6 billion of the total market value. These were deals covering businesses in several countries rather than direct acquisitions of standalone Romanian companies. Strategic investors remained the main buyers, accounting for 65 transactions, while financial investors were involved in 28. The number of deals involving financial investors increased by approximately 14% year-on-year. Romanian investors completed 35 transactions, representing around 38% of the total, compared with approximately 41% in the third quarter of 2025. “Political stability, a continued reduction in the budget deficit, and confirmation that inflation is stabilising or falling remain key factors for investor interest and for the valuations of local businesses,” said Marina Pavel, M&A director at PwC Romania. PwC also noted that a larger proportion of the quarter’s announced deals remained at the signing stage rather than being completed. This reflected both longer regulatory approval processes and more intense activity toward the end of the period.

data.title: Romania’s president expected to designate new PM candidate
data.description: The consultations are taking place after the Parliament rejected the government proposed by PM-designate Siegfried Mureșan on September 30, extending the political crisis that has lasted since the Ilie Bolojan government was toppled in May. Sources cited by Digi24 indicated that Dan has two favourites for the position: PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu and interim finance minister Alexandru Nazare. Grindeanu has repeatedly said that PSD is prepared to assume responsibility for forming a government, while also insisting that any government must have a transparent parliamentary majority behind it. Sorin Grindeanu has no explicit parliamentary majority behind him. A Grindeanu government would face the immediate problem of securing PNL support, given the party’s continued backing for Ilie Bolojan, who consolidated his internal position after May when his government was toppled by a no-confidence motion initiated by PSD and AUR. PSD could seek support from AUR – although AUR has no incentive to offer such support, but may engage in negotiations for visibility. Furthermore, such an arrangement is incompatible with president Dan’s stated opposition to bringing AUR into the ruling majority, on the grounds that this would risk Romania’s relations with its foreign partners. In practice, a Grindeanu government would therefore appear to require both a significant number of PNL lawmakers to break with their party’s position, and support from AUR and potentially lawmakers leaving its parliamentary group (thus bypassing the president's red line). A further issue of a full-fledged PSD government would be the fiscal policy. PSD has advocated measures aimed at stimulating economic activity and improving social outcomes. In the current context, however, a significant fiscal loosening would conflict with the consolidation requirements underpinning Romania’s sovereign ratings and could increase the risk of renewed fiscal slippage. Alexandru Nazare could offer a broader basis for parliamentary support. Although not necessarily an independent candidate, given his previous affiliation with PNL, Nazare is now perceived more as a technocrat, particularly after his recent role at the Finance Ministry and his engagement with international rating agencies. His current position would also give him continuity in discussions with the rating agencies at a critical moment for Romania’s sovereign credit profile. A Nazare government could potentially offer a compromise between PSD’s demand for domestic policy measures (no reforms) and the fiscal consolidation required to preserve Romania’s investment-grade rating. The difficulty would be reconciling the political demands of a future coalition with the need for structural measures that provide a lasting improvement in the budget balance. Other names circulating ahead of the consultations include Eugen Tomac, who was previously proposed by Dan but withdrew before a parliamentary vote, former Romanian ambassador to France Luca Niculescu, and Leonardo Badea, first deputy governor of the National Bank of Romania. Public reports have also mentioned other PNL figures among the names being considered. President Dan still pressures for the revival of the four-party centrist coalition. Following Mureșan’s failure in Parliament, Dan drew a red line around the participation of AUR in a future government. His argument has not been that AUR’s participation would be intrinsically unacceptable, but that bringing the party into government would endanger Romania’s relations with its foreign partners. This position has become one of the central constraints on the negotiations for a new ruling majority. Dan has also argued strongly against early elections, most recently saying that investors financing Romania’s deficit had sent him a message against such a scenario. The combination of the president’s opposition to snap polls, the absence of an explicit majority behind the leading candidates and the increasingly difficult negotiations among the parliamentary parties leaves the fourth nomination facing the same fundamental problem as the previous three: securing enough votes to actually form a government.

data.title: Romania’s ailing Mangalia shipyard up for sale at lower price
data.description: The previous auctions were held at the market value of EUR 184 million, excluding VAT, while the new starting price has been cut to EUR 138 million, according to News.ro . Paul Dieter Cîrlănaru, general director of CITR, told News.ro that if there are no offers at 75% of the market value, another auction can be organised with a starting price of 50% of the market value. However, the shipyard cannot ultimately be sold below EUR 84.15 million, excluding VAT, representing the liquidation value of the asset, according to the sale publication for the second auction term. The new procedure follows a challenge by Damen Holding BV, the main creditor of Damen Mangalia, against a decision by the Constanța Court allowing the modification of the shipyard's sale procedure. The initial procedure envisaged six monthly auctions, all starting at the market value of EUR 184 million. Damen Shipyards Mangalia entered insolvency on June 19, 2024, at the request of its parent company, Damen Holding BV, which claimed 69.5% of the shipyard's total debts recorded at the time. Together with other companies in the group, Damen controlled approximately 85% of the receivables.

data.title: Nova Power&Gas says it joined LNG memorandum at Romanian government’s request
data.description: The company’s statement, as reported by Economica.net and Profit.ro , came amid a political controversy triggered by reports in The Wall Street Journal and The Financial Times that US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle pressured Romania to buy American LNG and suggested that the US had been involved in the dismissal of the Ilie Bolojan government. Nova Power&Gas said it was invited to participate in the memorandum by representatives of Transgaz, the Romanian government and the Ministry of Energy, through State Secretary Cristian Bușoi. The company said it was approached as a last-minute solution because the memorandum had to be signed by both the gas transmission operator and a company authorised to import and export natural gas. NPG said it met those requirements, having subsidiaries in neighbouring countries and having imported natural gas mainly from Bulgaria in recent years. The company also said that no agreement, including a draft contract, was reached during the memorandum’s 90-day validity period. The memorandum expired on February 5, 2026, without resulting in a gas purchase agreement. NPG rejected the perception that US LNG would have been more expensive than gas available on the Romanian market. According to the company, the first proposal received from the Greek-American consortium would have resulted in a delivered price of EUR 30-35/MWh for 2026 and 2027, including transportation costs. By comparison, NPG said the domestic market price was EUR 65/MWh for 2026 and EUR 58/MWh for 2027. The company also said the gas covered by the memorandum would have been intended primarily for transit rather than domestic consumption. Purchases for Romania’s domestic market would have been considered only for the period after 2036, according to NPG. The statement came as questions continue over the circumstances surrounding the proposed LNG deal and the role of Romanian and US officials in discussions about potential purchases of American gas.

According to the company, the first proposal received from the Greek-American consortium would have resulted in a delivered price of EUR 30-35/MWh for 2026 and 2027, including transportation costs. By comparison, NPG said the domestic market price was EUR 65/MWh for 2026 and EUR 58/MWh for 2027. The company also said the gas covered by the memorandum would have been intended primarily for transit rather than domestic consumption. Purchases for Romania’s domestic market would have been considered only for the period after 2036, according to NPG. The statement came as questions continue over the circumstances surrounding the proposed LNG deal and the role of Romanian and US officials in discussions about potential purchases of American gas.

data.title: CFA Romania sees economic growth of up to 0.5% in 2027
data.description: The report, which will be presented in its third edition, indicated a year of modest economic recovery as Romania adjusts to the fading impact of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) and seeks new sources of growth, Economica.net reported. CFA Romania’s economists are examining whether investment supported by European funds can become a new growth engine as the consumption-based economic model loses its ability to sustain the same pace of development. The transition from the PNRR to cohesion funds and the ability of public investment to attract private capital will be essential for the quality of economic growth in 2027, according to the organisation. The outlook also pointed to continuing macroeconomic pressures. Fiscal consolidation, high financing needs, energy prices, pressures on the leu and the sovereign risk premium are expected to remain important factors for the Romanian economy next year.

data.title: Moody’s sees significant risk of snap elections in Romania, no 2027 budget by year-end
data.description: The rating agency also believes it is becoming increasingly unlikely that sufficient political support can be secured to adopt the 2027 budget before the end of this year. On September 30, Romania’s political deadlock deepened as Parliament failed to approve a new government for the third time since May , when the pro-European coalition government was dismissed. Despite a new round of cabinet talks scheduled to begin on October 5 and the president’s strong preference to avoid early elections, the latest impasse indicates that the likelihood of snap polls is significant, Moody’s said. The latest failure to form a government leads Moody’s to question the sustainability of Romania’s fiscal consolidation beyond 2026. While the fiscal adjustment has significantly exceeded expectations so far this year, further measures are needed to continue reducing Romania’s deficit, which remains the largest among EU member states. Moody’s questions the sustainability of the fiscal adjustment achieved so far. Data for the first eight months of 2026 showed a further narrowing of the cash deficit, to 2.9% of GDP from 4.5% in the same period of 2025, Moody’s admitted. However, the rating agency noted that much of the improvement reflected temporary restrictions on public-sector wages and social transfers, which reduced total spending by 0.7 percentage points year-on-year, as well as stronger-than-expected tax revenues, with VAT receipts up 25.2%. At the same time, Moody’s sees underlying spending pressures as remaining significant. Financing from the RRF has now ended, while pressure to increase spending on defence, public-sector wages and pensions continues to build. Moody’s therefore sees the political developments of the coming weeks as important in determining whether the fiscal adjustment achieved this year will prove sufficiently durable to support Romania’s sovereign credit profile. Other takes from Moody’s ad hoc comment. Rising interest costs are narrowing Romania’s fiscal space and complicating further consolidation. Romania’s interest bill has risen rapidly amid higher risk premia on international borrowing, weaker domestic demand and exchange-rate pressures affecting external debt servicing. Interest expenses reached RON42bn, or around EUR8bn and 2.2% of GDP, in 2025 and increased by 26.7% year-on-year through August 2026. The increase continues a multi-year trend of rising debt-service costs. Political uncertainty has already made domestic financing conditions less favourable. The average bid-to-cover ratio at September Treasury auctions was only 1.3x, falling to 0.9x for short-term maturities of up to one year. Exchange-rate movements add further pressure to debt-servicing costs and the current-account deficit, given that more than half of general government debt is denominated in foreign currencies. Romania’s gross financing needs of around EUR 55 billion this year also leave the sovereign dependent on continued market access at a time when political uncertainty remains elevated. Moody’s warning therefore came not so much from the deterioration of the 2026 fiscal numbers, which have been better than expected, as from the increasing difficulty of ensuring that this improvement can be maintained beyond the temporary measures underpinning it.

data.title: S&P affirms Romania rating, but risks remain to fiscal outlook
data.description: The decision is consistent with what can be regarded as a near-term baseline scenario in rating terms: that Romania will successfully form a government capable of adopting a credible budgetary framework for 2027-2028. However, the fluid political situation could threaten the reduction of the twin deficits – the country’s main rating vulnerability – and ultimately put the rating under pressure, the agency noted. S&P’s baseline scenario may be interpreted strictly in the context of its rating framework, alongside its upside and downside scenarios, rather than as an indication of the agency’s assessment of the likelihood of particular political or economic developments. In this context, the negative outlook reflects elevated implementation risks surrounding the consolidation of Romania’s public finances and the narrowing of its external deficits. The agency therefore sees significant downside risks to the current rating if the fiscal and external adjustment fails to proceed as envisaged. A prolonged government-formation process or failure to agree on a credible 2027-2028 budget framework may be expected to trigger sovereign rating reviews by all three major agencies in early 2027. The rating agency’s downside and upside scenarios also underline the importance of the 2027-2028 policy framework. On the downside, S&P warned that failure to implement a credible fiscal and policy path would jeopardise budgetary consolidation and could trigger broader pressures through deteriorating investor sentiment, higher funding costs and increased balance-of-payments pressures. The agency also said it could consider a downgrade if external pressures intensify. Conversely, S&P sees scope for an improvement in the rating outlook if Romania succeeds in narrowing both its external and fiscal deficits, supported by a credible medium-term policy plan, potentially anchored by broad-based political consensus, alongside a rebound in economic growth. The review came at a particularly volatile moment, both politically and economically, with risks stemming from domestic and external factors. S&P noted that Romania’s political landscape remains characterised by instability, while the lack of a functional government is undermining the predictability of reforms and clouding medium-term fiscal governance. The electoral cycle also creates additional fiscal risks, with S&P estimating that Romania’s fiscal deficits have historically widened by around 1.3% of GDP in election years. S&P’s macroeconomic scenario is optimistic compared with consensus expectations. The agency expects Romania’s economy to grow by 2.25% in 2027, driven by a recovery in consumption and a fading drag from fiscal consolidation, following an estimated 0.5% contraction in 2026. This compares with CFA Romania’s latest expectations, which, although not fully published, indicate growth of only around 0%-0.5% in 2027, according to information consulted by Economica.net. CFA analysts have questioned what will drive growth once the substantial stimulus provided by the RRF in recent years fades. S&P expects a rebound in private-sector investment to partly offset a decline of around 2% of GDP in public investment as EU inflows taper off. S&P’s fiscal scenario is consistent with the latest fiscal trajectory agreed by Romania and the European Commission under the Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP). The agency expects fiscal consolidation through 2027-2028 to remain anchored by the EDP. It forecasts the ESA deficit narrowing from 7.9% of GDP in 2025, following 9.3% in 2024, to 6.25% this year, 5.8% in 2027 and 5.0% in 2028. There is a direct correlation between S&P’s political baseline – under which Romania successfully forms a government that adopts a credible 2027-2028 budgetary framework – and its fiscal scenario. Again, however, this should be read in a rating context: S&P is effectively describing the fiscal path consistent with maintaining the current rating, rather than necessarily forecasting that these political and fiscal developments will occur. The agency also provided an indication of how such consolidation could be achieved. S&P expects the 2027 fiscal effort to focus primarily on the expenditure side, through controlled increases in public wages and pensions following a two-year freeze. An agreed framework for social spending indexation could help facilitate political cooperation, the agency says. At the same time, given the requirements of the EDP, S&P sees limited room for wage or pension increases to significantly outpace nominal GDP growth in 2027-2028. Romania’s external position is lagging behind the projected improvement in the fiscal balance, although S&P also pointed to positive factors such as the Neptun Deep offshore gas project. S&P forecasts Romania’s current-account deficit at 7.5% of GDP in 2026, narrowing only marginally to 7.0% in 2027 and remaining around 1 percentage point of GDP above the fiscal deficit through 2029. The agency attributes part of the persistence of the external deficit to structural external factors rather than simply to domestic consumption, notably rising interest payments on a substantially larger external debt stock. Although FDI and EU inflows are expected to finance around 50% of the current-account deficit on average in 2027-2029, S&P expects Romania’s external debt net of external liquid assets to rise from 52% of current-account receipts in 2025 to 60% by 2029. This leaves the external position as a significant vulnerability even as the fiscal deficit improves.

data.title: Romanian students win five medals at International Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad
data.description: Romanian students won three gold and two silver medals at the 2026 International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics, the Education Ministry announced. The 19th edition of the competition took place in Hanoi, Vietnam, from September 25 to October 5. Alexandru-Ioan Jicu of the Gheorghe Vrănceanu National College in Bacău, Teodor Bichir of the International Computer High School of Bucharest, and Robert-Cristian Amariei of the Sfântu Nicolae Theoretical High School in Gheorgheni, Harghita county, won gold medals. Meanwhile, Vlad Toncu of the Tudor Vianu National College of Computer Science in Bucharest and Vlad-Tudor Bolohan of the International Computer High School of Bucharest received silver medals. The competition brought together 315 students from 64 countries, the ministry said. Contestants completed five tests covering theory, telescope observations, planetarium work, data analysis, and teamwork. https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=1541059748058725&set=a.248573397307373

data.title: Thousands march for animal rights in Bucharest
data.description: Around 4,000 people joined an animal-rights protest in Bucharest on Sunday, October 4, according to Digi24 . The demonstration, held on World Animal Day, brought together campaigners and representatives of more than 70 animal-protection organisations from across Romania. Participants gathered outside the National Theatre in downtown Bucharest before marching toward Victoriei Square. Some travelled from cities including Iași, Timișoara, Constanța, Satu Mare, Târgu Jiu, Târgu Mureș, and Suceava, while others attended with their pets. “Their lives matter” and “We are their voice, the voice of animals” were among the slogans chanted during the march. https://www.facebook.com/asociatiasaveourpaws/posts/pfbid031BTSRu1sdfijBbjZS7wuUWhSkoaTnX7p19ZgYod16cN7PmnJiuZ6kwVEW52sgrHDl The protest was organised by the Together for Animals Federation alongside animal-welfare organisations. “We no longer want a country where animal suffering is normalised,” the groups said, as reported by Digi24. Campaigners called on the authorities to change the way stray animals are managed and give greater priority to sterilisation, including for owned pets. They argued that this would help reduce abandonment and uncontrolled breeding. The organisations also demanded an end to the euthanasia of stray animals. They claimed that at least 99,512 dogs had been killed in publicly funded shelters in recent years, while broader estimates cited by organisers put the number of euthanised dogs above 200,000. The protest also addressed the treatment of cats, farm animals, and wildlife. Participants highlighted the conditions experienced by poultry and other animals on farms, livestock transported for export, and mink and chinchillas killed for fur. https://www.facebook.com/sachevetclinic/posts/pfbid0tBXMT3CrA2aYCLLbWiB5SoxdutHnqxHX7wcbG3kz6MLUhvyZCA3CLx3kg9qpYnp2l

data.title: Poland, Romania Reject Ukraine Appeal for Grain Transit Help
data.description: Poland and Romania have rejected Ukraine’s request to increase agricultural transit corridors and secure €1.1 billion in transport subsidies to move trapped grain through Europe. data.title: SBU Drones Strike Su-35 and Su-34 Jets at Russian Airfield
data.description: Long-range drones operated by the Security Service of Ukraine’s (SBU) “Alpha” Special Operations Center struck an Su-35 fighter, an Su-34 bomber, and an ammunition depot at the Khanskaya military airfield in Russia’s Republic of Adygea, the SBU confirmed on Sunday, Oct. 4. The precision operation, conducted roughly 500 kilometers from Ukrainian territory, directly targets tactical aircraft utilized by Moscow to launch standoff guided aerial bomb strikes.

data.title: Ukraine to Deploy Small Missiles, Turrets Against Jet Drones, Zelensky Says
data.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will begin deploying domestically produced small missiles by late October and expanding automated .50-caliber gun turrets to counter Russian jet-powered strike drones. Speaking alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Kyiv on Sunday, Oct. 4, the leaders finalized a bilateral counter-drone agreement, while Merz emphasized that Moscow’s threats and ongoing drone attacks did not deter his high-level government and business delegation.

data.title: Germany Pledges €1.3B Defense Package During Merz Kyiv Visit
data.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a €1.3 billion assistance package in Kyiv on Sunday, Oct. 4, comprising €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for energy grid repairs. The leaders finalized 15 bilateral industrial pacts valued at over €8.5 billion, including a counter-drone agreement, while Merz revealed plans for a winter “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in Berlin with France and the UK.

data.title: Ukraine’s Science Under Fire: Russia Is Targeting Knowledge, People and the Future

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. data.description: President Jennifer Simons wil haast maken met de Wet Openbaarheid van Bestuur en de komst van een Ombudsman. data.title: Somohardjo: PL voelt zich goed in coalitie, problemen worden intern besproken

data.title: La B: Oriental es líder en soledad
data.description: El conjunto de La Paz igualó 0-0 con Colón, pero abrió un punto de diferencia sobre Plaza, que perdió ante Cerrito; Atenas de San Carlos ganó y está segundo. mientras que Miramar Misiones sacó un triunfo clave por el descenso.
